_comment: Registry of upstream data sources for the OurHike pipeline. Generated/updated by discover_sources.py - re-run that script rather than hand-editing urls here. A source discovery cannot see, because it is not an ArcGIS layer behind the Experience Builder app, is registered by hand and marked with a `kind`: discover_sources.py keeps entries it did not rediscover verbatim, so a hand-written entry survives a re-run. lib/source_registry.py is what reads `kind`, and an entry without one is an ArcGIS feature layer.

photo_licence._comment: The basis on which the Photo1..Photo10 images on the ATC facilities layers may be mirrored and served, recorded rather than assumed - CONTRIBUTING.md, 'A note on data and licences'. This is NOT a Creative Commons grant and must not be rendered as one: ATC holds the copyright, and what is recorded here is the permission to use them, not a licence to sublicense them onward. A club inheriting this project needs to re-confirm it in its own name rather than relying on this line.

atc_licence._comment: The basis on which DATA the Appalachian Trail Conservancy publishes on its own ArcGIS org and services may be reused - photo_licence's sibling, extended from the photos to the data layers by the maintainer's declaration of 2026-08-13 ('anything from the ATC is reusable', restated specifically for the FarOut-measured CSI water distances - #688). Scope, stated tightly: facts ATC itself publishes (half-mile points, the Campsite_Sustainability_Index water distances build_water_distance.py takes, whatever future ATC-org layer a change deliberately adopts). It does NOT cover documents the maintaining clubs publish (per-entry licence fields govern those, e.g. gatc_water_sources below), does NOT override editorial holdbacks that are about safety or partnership rather than licensing (CSI's user-created campsites stay unpublished - SOURCE_SURVEY.md §3b), and is not a grant to sublicense ATC's work onward.

sources.title: A.T. Trail Updates
sources.licence: Facts and a link only, and NOT a grant to mirror ATC's prose. What is published is the mile range, category, states, headline and ATC's own last-updated date, with a link back to their page - facts about the trail, which is a different thing from the paragraphs ATC wrote about them. #458 asked ATC directly what may be republished and was closed without asking, on the maintainer's judgement as an ATC trail volunteer; that decision settles the conservative version and not the broader one, so the body text stays on ATC's own page. A club inheriting this project needs to confirm this in its own name rather than relying on this line - the same footing as `photo_licence` above and the general question in https://github.com/OurHike/OurHike/issues/98.

freshness.notes: The RSS feed, used as a change signal and NOT as the content. Measured 2026-08-24: it held 3 items while the listing held 89 across ten paginated pages, so building the artifact from it would silently drop the most consequential closure (features/ATC_TRAIL_UPDATES.md, 'what the feed does not carry'). The 2026-08-09 version of this note read '3 items while the page showed 9'; the 9 was page one mistaken for the whole list, which is https://github.com/OurHike/OurHike/issues/945. It does carry an ETag that moves when ATC edits, which is all a freshness marker needs - WEAK (`W/"..."`) as measured 2026-08-24, where this note said 'strong' on 2026-08-12; check_freshness.py compares it verbatim and only asks whether it moved, but a weak validator lets the upstream change the bytes without changing the tag. The listing page itself is still not usable as the marker, and now for two reasons. The correction this note carried briefly on 2026-08-24 - 'it no longer 403s a scripted request, it answers 200' - was measured with curl and did not describe the pipeline's own client: re-measured the same day, ATC refuses the literal `python-requests/*` User-Agent with 403 and answers 200 to curl and to a named agent, so the original 2026-08-12 finding was right about check_freshness.py and still is. lib/atc_scrape.py reaches the listing only because it sets a User-Agent naming the project. On top of that, a HEAD on the listing returns neither an ETag nor a Last-Modified, so even an allowed request would give a marker of UNKNOWN forever.

sources.notes: Not fetched by fetch_all.py and has no data/raw/<key>.geojson - the build input is the reviewed file named in `reviewed_input`, which a human edits and a merged pull request releases (#460). The freshness marker is what tells that human ATC has published something since they last looked.

sources.title: GATC Water Sources (approach trail + Georgia A.T.)
sources.licence: Unstated - a free public download from GATC's own site, fetched for REVIEW AND CROSS-CHECKS ONLY. Nothing from this source reaches a published artifact until GATC answers a redistribution ask (CONTRIBUTING.md, 'A note on data and licences'; the ask is the same shape as https://github.com/OurHike/OurHike/issues/98 records for opentrail.org). WATER_SOURCES.md §4 sizes this document as 'a pilot-state candidate after an email' and notes its embedded title is 'GATC Water Update July 2020.xlsx', so the 2026-03 file may re-export older data - a second reason the ask precedes any publication.
sources.discovered_via: SOURCE_SURVEY.md §5's club sweep (the 'water-sources PDF (2026-03-02)' row); fetched and parsed live 2026-08-13 (#669). Registered by hand - discover_sources.py walks the Experience Builder app and this source is not in it.
sources.notes: Fetched by fetch_club_pdfs.py to data/raw/club_pdfs/<key>.pdf (never by fetch_all.py), parsed by lib/club_pdfs.py to <key>.json beside it: 65 rows (4 approach trail + 61 A.T., measured on the live PDF 2026-08-13, agreeing with WATER_SOURCES.md §4's count) of GATC mile point + entry text. The PDF's text layer stores each printed row as one string, so the 'Source Name' and 'Distance Off AT' columns arrive fused and are kept that way rather than split by guesswork - lib/club_pdfs.py's docstring holds the measurement.

sources.title: OSM water point sources (fourteen A.T. states)
sources.licence: ODbL 1.0 - attribution and share-alike, the terms the self-built basemap already complies with; the client's credits screen names OpenStreetMap and each published water point's description carries 'Mapped by OpenStreetMap contributors'. This is the openly licensed half of #529's water answer - no ask pending, unlike the ATC and club rows above.
sources.discovered_via: WATER_SOURCES.md's census for #529 (spike_osm_water_census.py) measured OSM point sources within 250 m of 26% of shelters trail-wide and 40% in the south, against 8% for the shipped supply. Registered by hand - discover_sources.py walks the Experience Builder app and this source is not in it.
sources.notes: Fetched by fetch_osm_water.py to data/raw/osm_water.geojson (never by fetch_all.py): nodes tagged natural=spring, amenity=drinking_water, man_made=water_tap or man_made=water_well across the fourteen Geofabrik state extracts export_basemap.py already downloads - 7,574 nodes on the first full scan (2026-08-13). No freshness entry on purpose: Geofabrik republishes the extracts daily, so a changed-marker would always say yes (export_basemap.py's docstring holds the reasoning; the fetch is skip-if-present with --refetch). export_poi.py folds these into poi_type water at low confidence, dropping each point within 25 m of an opentrail water point as the same node arriving twice.

sources.title: 3D Hydrography Program (3DHP)
sources.licence: Public domain, as a work of the United States government — the whole USGS hydrography column (WATER_SOURCES.md §5). Attribution is courtesy rather than obligation, and the client's credits screen already names USGS for NHD.

freshness.notes: The distinct `workunitid` values 3DHP's flowline layer returns for boxes on the trail. `NHD` is 3DHP saying, in its own field, that these lines are the retired dataset republished rather than anything it has surveyed - measured 2026-08-14 at five points spread along the trail from North Carolina (mile 110) to New Hampshire (mile 1,868), every one of them `NHD`. When that stops being the answer, 3DHP has resurveyed the corridor and the migration this pipeline is deliberately not doing becomes worth costing. Changing `recorded` is how a person acknowledges having looked; nothing writes it automatically.

sources.discovered_via: WATER_SOURCES.md §5, following USGS's retirement of the NHD on 2023-10-01. Registered by hand - discover_sources.py walks ATC's Experience Builder app and this is not in it.
sources.notes: Nothing fetches this. It is registered because the pipeline's water derivation (fetch_trail_water.py) reads a dataset USGS no longer maintains, and this is where its replacement will appear. Measured 2026-08-14: for the corridor, 3DHP IS NHD - identical geometry (1,265 flowlines in a box in central Virginia against NHD's 1,265, same vertex count, worst-case separation 0.086 mm) and identical springs (1,796 features, every one within 1 m of an NHD spring) - with the perennial/intermittent FCode collapsed away into an undifferentiated `Channel Line`. Migrating now would trade the only structured seasonality signal the pipeline has for the same geometry, so the entry holds a watch instead of a fetch.

NDMC's permission page (read 2026-08-15) explicitly allows reproducing the MAP given the credit line below, and is silent on redistributing the underlying data - which is what conditions/drought.json does. Recorded on the maintainer's declaration of 2026-08-15, the same footing as atc_licence above: a federally co-produced dataset published for open download is reusable with the required credit. Scope: the weekly USDM class polygons and nothing else. It is NOT a grant to sublicense NDMC's work onward, and it does not extend to any other NDMC or drought.gov product.

usdm_licence.attribution: The U.S. Drought Monitor is jointly produced by the National Drought Mitigation Center at the University of Nebraska-Lincoln, the United States Department of Agriculture, the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration and the National Aeronautics and Space Administration. oprhp_licence._comment: The basis on which the four oprhp_* layers above may be fetched, and the bar their data has to clear before any of it is republished to hikers. CORRECTED 2026-08-24 (#950). This block previously said OPRHP's terms were UNSTATED and that the item's licenseInfo was 'a no-warranty disclaimer'. THAT WAS WRONG, and the way it was wrong is worth recording: the licenseInfo was read through a 200-character truncation on 2026-08-18, which cut off exactly at the sentence where the disclaimer ends and the actual terms begin. The full field is 1,095 characters of plain text on AGOL item a89dcd37f8bc41929e490dacd872e288 (the item whose `url` is the registered NY_State_Parks_Trails FeatureServer), re-read in full 2026-08-24 and quoted verbatim in `terms_verbatim` below. SO THERE IS A GRANT, WITH TWO CONDITIONS ON IT. Reuse is permitted; attribution to OPRHP is REQUIRED on 'any maps, reports, or other materials created using OPRHP data'; and the data is provided 'for informational and NON-COMMERCIAL purposes'. The second condition is the one that needs a human: features/PRICING_MODEL.md designs a paid thru-hike pass and regional passes, so whether shipping these lines inside OurHike is a non-commercial use is a judgement about the product, not a fact about the layer. The reading that says yes is PRICING_MODEL.md's own pricing value #5 - the trail line is in the tier that 'stay[s] free forever, for everyone, regardless of ability to pay', and what is sold is the convenience layer above it. That reading is not recorded here as settled, because nobody with authority to settle it has written it down.
oprhp_licence.author: New York State Office of Parks, Recreation and Historic Preservation
oprhp_licence.license: Reuse permitted with attribution to OPRHP; non-commercial condition determined satisfied by the maintainer 2026-08-24
oprhp_licence.terms_verbatim: The data are dynamic and may change over time. Although every effort has been made to ensure the accuracy of information, NY State Office of Parks, Recreation and Historic Preservation (OPRHP) makes no representations or warranties, express or implied, as to the accuracy, reliability, or completeness of the data and assumes no responsibility or legal liability for its use. The data are for informational purposes only and are not intended for or suitable for legal, engineering, surveying, or site-specific decision-making. The user is responsible for ensuring the accuracy and appropriateness of any use of the data and assumes all risks associated with its use. The data and applications are provided for informational and non-commercial purposes. Any maps, reports, or other materials created using OPRHP data must include proper credit and attribution to the NY State Office of Parks, Recreation and Historic Preservation (OPRHP). By accessing or using the OPRHP data and applications, you agree to be bound by the above terms of use and failure to do so constitutes a misuse of the data.
oprhp_licence.attribution_required: New York State Office of Parks, Recreation and Historic Preservation (OPRHP)
oprhp_licence.basis: OPRHP's own published item terms (read 2026-08-24, quoted verbatim above), plus the maintainer's determination of the same date that OurHike is a non-commercial use within them. THE REASONING, recorded because a determination nobody can inspect is worth no more than an assertion: features/PRICING_MODEL.md's pricing value #1 keeps the core map, water, shelters, GPS, elevation, closures and warnings 'free forever, for everyone, regardless of ability to pay', and a trail line is squarely in that tier. What OurHike sells is the planning and community layer above it - value #5's 'a maintained, polished experience on top of open data'. So OPRHP's data itself is given to hikers for nothing. THE COUNTER-READING, stated so nobody has to reconstruct it: the app as a whole does take money, and a stricter reading of 'non-commercial purposes' looks at the product rather than at the tier. This block records that the maintainer weighed that and decided; it does not record that OPRHP agrees, because OPRHP has not been asked this specific question yet.
oprhp_licence.open_question: https://github.com/OurHike/OurHike/issues/769 - OPRHP's own answer would replace the maintainer's determination above with theirs, and is still worth having. Until then the determination is what this ships on. If OPRHP reads it the other way, the remedy is one field per source and a re-run, which is the whole reason the gate is a registry field rather than a code path.

nynjtc_licence._comment: The basis on which the two nynjtc_* layers above may be fetched, and the bar their data has to clear before any of it is republished to hikers. NYNJTC's terms are genuinely UNSTATED, and this was re-checked properly on 2026-08-24 after the same truncation bug that had misread OPRHP's (see oprhp_licence): both AGOL items were fetched whole and matched to the registered FeatureServer URLs - 55350d7014c746949809bde71e373d67 ('Long Path - 2025 Fall') and aa7e805d911546a189d47b7263c6e686 ('Highlands Trail in NY & NJ - Fall 2025'). Both carry an EMPTY licenseInfo and an EMPTY accessInformation - zero characters, not a disclaimer and not a grant - and both services return an empty copyrightText. Public and queryable is not a reuse grant (SOURCE_SURVEY.md's rule 3, 'licensed beats good'), and an absent licence is more restrictive than OPRHP's stated one rather than less: with nothing said, ordinary copyright is what applies. The sharper point one registration cannot blur: these two are NYNJTC's PUBLIC EXTRACTS, and SOURCE_SURVEY.md §5's verdict on the wider network stands - the full NYNJTC trail network is deliberately withheld and is 'an agreement, not a scrape'. Registering the extracts is not a step toward taking the rest. The maintainer's NYNJTC conversation (declared 2026-08-18 on issue #768) covers both.

nynjtc_licence.basis: Maintainer authorisation, 2026-08-24, on the maintainer's own reading that these are openly published datasets. THE SAME FOOTING atc_licence AND photo_licence ALREADY USE, and worth being precise about what it is and is not: it is the maintainer deciding, as the person who carries the consequence, that publishing NYNJTC's two PUBLIC EXTRACTS is acceptable. It is NOT a grant from NYNJTC, who have stated nothing - their items carry an empty licenseInfo and an empty accessInformation, verified whole 2026-08-24 - so ordinary copyright is the default this decision is taken against. WHAT IT DOES NOT TOUCH: SOURCE_SURVEY.md §5's verdict on the full NYNJTC network stands unchanged - 'an agreement, not a scrape'. This authorisation covers the two public extracts and nothing else, and must not be read as precedent for the network.
nynjtc_licence.open_question: https://github.com/OurHike/OurHike/issues/768 - NYNJTC's own answer should replace the maintainer's authorisation with their stated terms, the way atc_licence's open question reads. A club that inherits this project needs to re-confirm it in its own name rather than relying on this line.

reaches_hikers_comment: Why every source entry carries `reaches_hikers` (#927). The sources screen names the organizations whose data is on a hiker's phone, under the terms each one set - so it has to know which registered sources actually SHIP, and that fact lived only in prose inside each entry's `licence` string ('fetched for REVIEW AND CROSS-CHECKS ONLY', 'nothing from this source reaches a published artifact until...'). A screen that decided by reading those sentences would print a licence claim for data nobody publishes the first time one was reworded. So it is a field: true means an exporter reads this source and its data reaches a release, false means registered-but-not-shipped, for any reason - review-only pending a licence answer (gatc_water_sources, every oprhp_*), watched-only (usgs_3dhp), or registered and not yet wired to anything (bridges, at_treadway, per pipeline/README.md). It is NOT a licence judgement and does not replace one: a source can be freely licensed and still not ship. export_sources.py refuses to run if any entry lacks the field, so a newly registered source cannot reach a hiker's screen by defaulting into it.
